official.deadline_note: No fixed closing date: applications can be submitted online throughout the year and should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the conference.
official.application_cycle: Rolling - online applications are accepted throughout the year
official.status_note: The scheme page states that applications can be submitted online throughout the year, uploaded at least three months before the due date of the conference; applications submitted after participation and presentation are not entertained or considered in any case.
benefits: Financial assistance covering air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance costs for the period of stay abroad and registration fee up to US$200
Up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit for regular faculty

Full financial assistance considered for SC/ST categorised faculties, persons with benchmark disability, and PG, doctoral and postdoctoral researchers without salary protection, as well as faculties from ICSSR Research Institutes and Recognised Institutes
Preference for younger scholars, scholars attending a conference or seminar for the first time, and scholars from remote and backward areas
eligibility: Faculties with regular service in publicly funded universities, deemed-to-be universities, colleges, Institutes of National Importance as defined by MoE/UGC, and ICSSR Research Institutes or Recognised Institutes, holding a PhD degree
Post-Graduate (regular), PhD and PDF scholars in social science disciplines in the advanced stage of their studies or research

Independent scholars having served as civil servants, officers from the defence services and other professionals with a social science perspective, with not less than 20 years of regular service and demonstrable research experience through books, research papers, reports or policy documents
Only applications where the paper for oral presentation has been accepted by the organiser through a formal invite; a simple email is not a formal invite
Scholars invited for poster presentation, to chair a session, as conveners or rapporteurs, or to attend a workshop, training, refresher or summer/winter course are not eligible
A scholar who has already availed of the facility can apply again after three years, and the award may be given twice in a lifetime
requirements: A formal invitation letter from the conference organiser, submitted along with the application
Submission of the full-length paper to be presented, which is mandatory and should be in English or Hindi
Online application at least three months before the due date of the conference, followed by the hard copy of the application
Air tickets to be purchased only through M/s Ashoka Travels and Tours (ATT), M/s Balmer Lawrie & Company Ltd (BLCL) or IRCTC
The expenditure will be reimbursed on submission of the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and a report on the participation
documents: Online application submitted through the ICSSR applicant portal at https://app.icssr.org/
Formal invitation letter from the conference organisers
Full-length paper to be presented, in English or Hindi
Hard copy of the application with all documents sent to the In-charge, ICG Division, Indian Council of Social Science Research, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, JNU Institutional Area, New Delhi 110067

For the grant release after the visit: original boarding pass, certificate of attendance or participation, statement of expenditure and a detailed report on participation in the conference, with copies of air tickets, visa-stamped and visa-payment receipts and registration-fee receipt
selection_criteria: Applications are initially scrutinised by the ICSSR Secretariat

An Expert Committee reviews the applications on the basis of the research background of the applicant, the quality of the paper and the academic credentials of the organising institution and the conference

Invitations from global subject associations, reputed international organisations, universities and institutions are preferred, with due consideration to the peer-review process of the conference organisers; the recommendations of the Expert Committee are then placed before the Research Committee/Council for final approval
coverage: Maintenance costs for the period of stay abroad, not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
Registration fee up to US$200, with scholars encouraged to apply for exemption from the registration fee under special circumstances
application_method: Obtain a formal invitation to present an oral paper at an international conference abroad
Submit the online application at https://app.icssr.org/ at least three months before the due date of the conference
Send the hard copy of the application with all documents to the In-charge, ICG Division, ICSSR, New Delhi 110067
After the visit, submit the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and participation report for reimbursement
official.application_route: Online application via the ICSSR portal plus a hard copy to the ICG Division, at least three months before the conference
official.citizenship_residency: Indian scholars in regular service at eligible Indian institutions, or postgraduate, doctoral and postdoctoral scholars in Indian social science disciplines, or eligible independent senior professionals
official.international_eligibility: No - the scheme funds Indian scholars travelling to conferences abroad
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Social science disciplines only: sociology and social anthropology, political science and public administration, economics, international studies, social geography and population studies, commerce and management, social psychology, education, social linguistics and socio-cultural studies, law and international law, national security and strategic studies, and other allied social science disciplines including interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary research
official.research_requirement: The paper for oral presentation must be accepted by the organiser through a formal invite after its review process; a full-length paper is mandatory; co-authored papers give priority to the first author, with No Objection Certificates from second authors where applicable
official.duration: Period of stay abroad not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
official.description: ICSSR's travel grant gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad, covering air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance costs for the stay and registration fee up to US$200 - up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit for regular faculty, with full assistance considered for specified categories.
official.english_requirement: The full-length paper to be presented is mandatory and should be either in English or Hindi.

not_confirmed: funding_amount (no fixed monetary figure is published - assistance is a percentage or share of the actual cost of the visit)
living_cost_coverage as a separately published benefit (maintenance costs are covered within the cost of the visit)
verification.notes: The coverage list (air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance costs, registration fee up to US$200), the 50 percent rule for regular faculty, the full-assistance categories, the three-month pre-conference submission rule and the three permitted travel agencies were confirmed both on the ICSSR scheme page and in the ICSSR Travel Grant Guidelines document dated 21-08-26 published on the same domain; no fixed monetary amount is published.

applicant_utility.summary: Timing is everything: the application must be uploaded at least three months before the conference's due date, and any application submitted after you have already attended is void - there is no post-hoc route. This is a reimbursement-style grant rather than a fixed award, so until ICSSR approves you cannot know the amount, and you must be prepared to fund the ticket first. Remember the once-in-three-years and twice-in-a-lifetime limits, and that only oral-paper invitations count - posters, session chairs, conveners and rapporteurs and workshop attendance are excluded.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Regular social science faculty and advanced PhD scholars with an oral-paper invitation to a peer-reviewed international conference, whose topic and organising institution carry academic weight.
application_readiness_checklist: Count back three months from the conference's own deadline and diary the ICSSR submission earlier than that
Obtain a formal invitation letter, not an email, showing the paper has been accepted for oral presentation
Prepare the full-length paper in English or Hindi in final form
Check whether you have already drawn this facility: another application is possible only after three years, and at most twice in a lifetime
Book the air ticket through Ashoka Travels and Tours, Balmer Lawrie or IRCTC only, and in economy class
Keep every original - boarding pass, visa receipts, registration-fee receipt, attendance certificate - for the final release
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the conference, which ICSSR will not entertain in any case
An invitation that is only an email, which is not treated as a formal invite
Poster presentations, session chairing, convenerships, rapporteur roles and workshops, which are ineligible
Co-authored papers where the applicant is not the first author and No Objection Certificates are missing
Missing the full-length paper, which is mandatory
Choosing the wrong discipline - only social science subjects and listed allied disciplines qualify
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining share of the visit cost for regular faculty (up to 50 percent is covered), plus registration fees above US$200 and any items outside the published list such as excess baggage.
document_audit: The hard copy to the ICG Division in New Delhi is as important as the online submission, so courier it in time
Reimbursement runs on originals: a scanned boarding pass is not accepted
If you are applying for a fee waiver from the organisers, mention it - ICSSR encourages exemption applications
For doctoral and postdoctoral applicants, evidence of advanced stage and of not having salary protection matters for the full-assistance category
alerts: Applications are not entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation, so never travel on the hope of retroactive approval
Travel bookings outside ATT, BLCL or IRCTC are not reimbursed
The scheme is rolling, so a strong invitation can be filed in any month as long as the three-month rule holds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure the oral-paper invitation, submit online at app.icssr.org plus a hard copy to the ICG Division at least three months ahead, attend, then claim with originals.

official.deadline_central_display: 31 October 2026 (student application deadline for academic year 2026-27)
official.deadline_note: For AY 2026-27 the scheme opened on 1 June 2026; defective application verification closes on 15 November 2026, institute verification on 15 November 2026 and DNO/SNO/MNO verification on 30 November 2026.
official.status_note: The National Scholarship Portal lists the AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for girl students (Technical Degree) as open for AY 2026-27 with student applications open until 31 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a lump sum 'towards payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipments, softwares etc.'; no other additional grant is payable in lieu of hostel charges and medical charges.
benefits: Rs. 50,000 per annum for every year of study, as a lump sum towards payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipments, softwares etc.
Payable for a maximum of 4 years for first-year admitted students and a maximum of 3 years for second-year admitted students through lateral entry
Paid through DBT mode on an annual basis after selection
No documentary proof need to be attached for the above while availing benefits
eligibility: The girl candidate must be admitted to the first year of a degree level course, or to the second year of a degree level course through lateral entry, in any of the AICTE-approved institutions of the respective year
A maximum of two girl children per family are eligible
Family income from all sources should not be more than Rs. 8 lakh per annum during the current financial year, and a valid income certificate issued by the State/UT Government must be enclosed
The gap period between the year of passing the qualifying examination and the session of admission in the degree course should not be more than two years
requirements: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal after initiation of the application process and the notice published on the AICTE website
The host institution where the candidate is studying is required to verify the online application
The Department of Technical Education (DTE) of the respective State/UT verifies these applications as a second level of scrutiny
Only verified online applications will be considered for the award; incomplete applications are summarily rejected
documents: Valid income certificate issued by the State/UT Government showing family income from all sources not exceeding Rs. 8 lakh per annum
Mark sheet of the qualifying 10+2 or equivalent examination, which determines the merit list
Institute verification of the online application on the National Scholarship Portal
Second-level verification by the Department of Technical Education of the respective State/UT
selection_criteria: Selection is carried out solely on the basis of merit of the qualifying examination, i.e. the percentage of marks obtained in the 10+2 or equivalent examination
State and UT-wise merit lists are prepared as per the number of scholarships allotted
Ties are broken first by the percentage of marks in the 10th examination and then by the elder age of the candidate
Reservation as per Government of India norms, with vacant reserved seats transferred to the General Category
coverage: Rs. 50,000 per annum as a lump sum towards college fee, computer, stationeries, books, equipments and softwares
No additional grant in lieu of hostel charges and medical charges
application_method: Complete the one-time registration on the National Scholarship Portal and apply for the AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for girl students (Technical Degree) for AY 2026-27
Upload the State/UT-issued income certificate and the qualifying-examination mark sheet before 31 October 2026
Have the application verified by the host institution and then by the State/UT DTE
For renewal, submit the passing certificate or mark sheet together with a letter from the Head of the Institution through the NSP portal
official.application_route: Online application on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) with institute and DTE verification
official.citizenship_residency: Indian girl students admitted to AICTE-approved institutions; the scheme is implemented within India and no separate citizenship or residency rule is published
official.international_eligibility: No - the scheme is for girl students admitted to AICTE-approved institutions in India
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Technical degree (first year) or second year through lateral entry in an AICTE-approved institution; a separate Pragati scheme exists for technical diploma students
official.duration: Up to 4 years for first-year admitted students and up to 3 years for second-year admitted students through lateral entry
official.description: The AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for girl students assists girls pursuing technical education with Rs. 50,000 per annum as a lump sum for every year of study - up to four years for first-year entrants and three years for lateral-entry students - for a maximum of two girls per family with family income from all sources not exceeding Rs. 8 lakh per annum, applied for on the National Scholarship Portal.
official.program_type: Government scholarship for women in technical education

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage as a direct fee reimbursement
current number of scholarships beyond the guidelines figure of 5,000 per annum for the degree scheme (the catalogue figure of 10,000 could not be reconciled with these guidelines)
verification.notes: The Rs. 50,000 per annum amount, the Rs. 8 lakh income ceiling, the two-girls-per-family rule, the four-year and three-year duration rules, the DBT payment mode, the merit procedure and the 5,000 earmarked scholarships (with an additional open pool for 13 UTs and North-Eastern states) were confirmed in AICTE's official scheme guidelines linked from the National Scholarship Portal; the NSP scheme listing confirms the AY 2026-27 window (open 1 June 2026, student deadline 31 October 2026, verification deadlines 15 and 30 November 2026).

applicant_utility.summary: Everything hinges on three numbers: two girls per family, Rs. 8 lakh per year maximum family income, and your 10+2 percentage, because selection is purely on that exam with 10th-standard marks and age only as tie-breakers. Apply on the National Scholarship Portal by 31 October 2026 and then make sure your institution actually verifies it - an unverified application is not considered even if perfect. Since payment is a single annual lump sum of Rs. 50,000 that also covers books, computer and stationery, treat it as a one-off yearly top-up rather than monthly support.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year or lateral-entry girl students in AICTE-approved technical degree institutions from families with all-source income below Rs. 8 lakh per annum.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your year of admission qualifies: first-year or second-year through lateral entry only, and that the gap since passing 10+2 is within two years
Check that no more than one sister in your family is already drawing the scholarship, since two girls per family is the cap
Get the State or UT government income certificate issued for the current financial year, below Rs. 8 lakh from all sources
Complete NSP one-time registration and apply for AY 2026-27 before 31 October 2026
Follow up with the institute office for NSP verification, then the State/UT DTE second-level scrutiny
Diarise 15 November 2026 for defective and institute verification and 30 November 2026 for the DNO/SNO/MNO stage
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications, which are summarily rejected regardless of merit
An institute that never verifies the online application, so only verified applications are considered
A third girl sibling in the family qualifying, breaching the two-per-family cap
Family income above Rs. 8 lakh from any source during the current financial year
Holding any other scholarship, stipend, salary or emolument, which discontinues the award and requires full refund
Failing to get promoted, which forfeits the scholarship, or a CGPA being used incorrectly - conversion is CGPA x 9.5
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Hostel charges and medical charges, which carry no additional grant, and any living or travel expenses.
document_audit: The income certificate must be a State/UT government document for the current financial year, not a self-declaration
Merit is computed from the 10+2 or equivalent percentage, so keep that mark sheet exact
For renewal you must upload the passing certificate or mark sheet plus a letter from the Head of the Institution through NSP
Provisional merit-list queries must be raised within one month of publication; payment queries within six months
alerts: Awarding of this scholarship does not entitle the student to any other scholarship; if you win another, refund to AICTE via demand draft payable to the Member Secretary, AICTE at New Delhi
The quota is distributed State and UT-wise, with an additional open pool for 13 UTs and North-Eastern states, so competition varies sharply by domicile
There is a separate Pragati scheme for technical diploma students with the same pattern, so confirm which version your course falls under
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on NSP, apply for AY 2026-27 before 31 October 2026 with income certificate and 10+2 marks, then institute and DTE verification, then DBT payment.
